text:
mrunal: Hey team, Acme reported a sudden p99 increase for streaming calls only (SSE). Non-streaming endpoints look fine. Observed TTFB jump from ~40ms -> ~1.8s. Can we triage?

lina: noted, linking ticket #ACME-588. Any recent infra changes in the proxy/flush side?

igor: we rolled a proxy tuning patch yesterday that bumps coalescing window from 5ms -> 20ms for throughput. Could be related.

mrunal: that aligns. Customer says it started ~03:10 UTC. Our deploy window was 02:50 UTC.

sam: logs from edge (eu-west-1) show higher time-to-first-byte on SSE connections. Sample: 
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:05Z] conn_id=abcd1234 path=/v1/chat/stream method=POST recv_headers=12ms first_chunk=1823ms total=3.1s
```

lina: hmm. non-stream POST to same model: 
```
[2026-03-16T03:12:06Z] conn_id=efgh5678 path=/v1/chat sync=true recv_headers=10ms resp=45ms total=120ms
```

igor: looks like chunk flush/coalesce is holding the first chunk. Need to confirm whether this is proxy-level coalesce or runtime KV/cache warmup.

eng-rtg: I can instrument kernel selection logs at 03:10->03:20 for the runtime. If coalesce is the culprit, runtime shouldn't block first chunk that long.

mrunal: quick repro steps from customer (they used SSE):
1) curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-xl","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'
2) measure time to first `data:` event.

sam: I ran that from our eu-west node, saw TTFB ~1.6s, and increased p99 across ~30% of connections.

lina: can we confirm if HTTP/2 clients show same behavior? Customer said mobile (h2) saw less impact vs SSE.

igor: initial observation: SSE paths go through proxy coalescer module that batches small writes. H2 path uses multiplexed frames so coalescing less aggressive. So likely change to coalesce window explains SSE-only spike.

mrunal: mitigation proposals:
- roll back proxy coalesce window to 5ms (fast mitigation), OR
- add override for streaming routes: force flush header chunk immediately, OR
- fallback: return non-streaming response for detected pathological clients (last resort).

eng-rtg: rollback is quick (release 2026.03.15-proxy-tuning). Can stage to eu-west first.

sam: while rollback happens, can we add an observability metric for first-chunk-latency by transport (SSE vs H2) and route? Want to show delta.

lina: creating a dashboard tile + alert for >= 500ms TTFB p95 on streaming routes. Also will surface to customer success.

ops-bot: deploy started: revert-proxy-coalesce-window -> in_progress (job 4521). ETA ~7m.

mrunal: thanks. After rollback, let's run the curl repro 10x and collect percentiles. Also check whether dedicated customers on same pool saw impact.

igor: follow-up note: if coalesce is needed for throughput, long-term we can implement adaptive coalesce: increase window when CPU underutilized and lower it per-route when streaming alpha client detected.

sam: confirmed: after rollback finished (03:29 UTC) quick check shows SSE TTFB back to ~35-60ms on sample runs. p99 improved to ~120ms within 10m.

mrunal: good. I'll draft a postmortem and recommend route-specific override + better canary for proxy perf flags.

lina: assigning PM/ops action items in ACME-588. Customer notified of mitigation. :white_check_mark:
